title: Build the Mermaid rendering mod with a bundled renderer
description: Add hooks/register.tsx, a bundled renderer/render.mjs built from beautiful-mermaid, and a vendored mermaid.js for the browser view, per the design in opum-doc docs/reference/operator-questions-skill-design.md at opum-doc origin/main 1312f0c, section Changes this needs in plain-english-styles item 8 and the Rendering the diagrams section. It renders Unicode in the terminal and Svg on desktop, VS Code and mobile, with a local HTML fallback. Built and proved on the terminal and the desktop app.

acceptanceCriteria.text: hooks/register.tsx installs a ui.render hook on the AssistantMessage site and renderer/render.mjs is committed so a git install needs no npm install
A vendored mermaid.js ships for the browser view and loads under strict security with a no-network Content-Security-Policy
A supported diagram draws in place and an unsupported type shows its source plus an Open diagram button
A streaming unclosed fence stays as source until the closing backticks arrive
A diagram wider than bodyColumns falls back to the browser view, never to wrapped art
With neither bun nor node on PATH the mod keeps the source and shows a line naming what is missing
ctrl+o still shows the stored source
The bundled helper ships the licence texts: beautiful-mermaid and mermaid under MIT, ELK.js under EPL-2.0

finalSummary:
The Mermaid rendering mod shipped in PR opum-ai/plain-english-styles#45. That pull request was merged without closing the task, so PES-10 read In Progress with nothing in flight; this tracker-only close records the evidence for its eight acceptance criteria and moves it to Done. Only the task record changes; no code rides along.

Criterion 7 (ctrl+o still shows the stored source) is the one with no test of ours. The mod returns a rewrite on the ui.render AssistantMessage site, and the plugin API types document what a rewrite does: claude-code.d.ts, the AssistantMessage doc comment (lines 9853-9858), states that a rewrite changes the drawing and leaves the stored message alone (ctrl+o). ctrl+o therefore shows the stored message - the original Mermaid fence source. Verified by reading that file this session; it is a documented engine contract, not a test we ran.

Criteria 1 and 8: the delivered files are on dev (hooks/register.tsx, renderer/render.mjs, renderer/vendor/mermaid.min.js, renderer/licenses/). Criteria 2-6: hooks/register.test.tsx, 21 plugin tests, including the width boundary both ways and the still-streaming fence.

Gates on the close head: lore check 24 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings; npm --prefix harness test 262 pass / 0 fail; claude plugin test . 21 pass / 0 fail; claude plugin validate . passes with one pre-existing warning; node harness/src/cli.mjs audit, all 12 checks agree. This repository has no required checks configured, so the local gates are the gate.
